assessment: This important study provides convincing data in support of the conclusion that weak but not strong fear memories are more easily modified using behavioral and pharmacological approaches potentially as a result of differential connectivity with the amygdala showing greater connectivity through the brain in weak compared to strong memories. The scope of the paper would be strengthened if both sexes were examined and more varied definitions of weak vs. strong memories were used. This paper is of interest to behavioral and neuroscience researchers studying learning, memory, and/or neural networks.
